Subject: Deployment safeguards & observed SLA thresholds - follow-up

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks to help us recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

1) Production SLOs you mentioned: 99.95% availability target and 95th percentile latency < 120ms for synchronous inference on 512-token requests. Is that still the target across all endpoints?
2) Peak concurrency: ~1200 QPS for the authentication service during morning batch window (we heard 800–1.2k). Can you confirm the expected sustained QPS and any burst patterns?
3) Data boundaries: PHI will flow through the model in certain flows. You flagged SOC2 + customer contractual controls as mandatory.
4) Isolation preferences: you said the Security team prefers dedicated resources if we can guarantee no co-tenancy—is that a requirement or a strong preference that could be met with a Private VPC?

Next steps from Redwood:
- I attached a short matrix (redwood-deployment-comparison-20270614.pdf) that maps cost/latency/reliability tradeoffs and our recommended configuration for each mode.
- Can you share a sanitized sample of traffic (token length distribution + QPS timeline) and a network diagram that shows whether inference traffic traverses a customer-managed NAT/GW? The medigen-network-sketch.png placeholder will help our infra team size the Dedicated pools.

Proposed schedule:
- Procurement intro + SOW review: Tue 6/15 (30m)
- Technical call with your security & network lead: Wed 6/16 (45m)

If you prefer, I can loop in Camila (solutions architect) to run through the eviction/isolation controls and Ben (sales engineer) for the performance guarantees.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

Subject: Re: Deployment safeguards & observed SLA thresholds - follow-up

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Yes, 99.95% availability and P95 < 120ms is our bar for patient-facing requests. Internal batch/analytics can tolerate higher latency.
- Sustained QPS expectation: 900–1,100 during peak; bursts to 1.5k for short windows (under 2 minutes) when billing cycles complete.
- PHI gating: must be encrypted in transit and at rest; customer-managed KMS preferred but we can accept Redwood-managed with a contractual KMS key wrap if needed.
- Isolation: Security's language is "no co-tenant access to memory/KV cache"—they are skeptical of shared GPU tenancy even with strong virtualization. That said, if Dedicated can be provisioned as isolated GPU pools (no other customers on same card), that might satisfy them.

I'll ping our network lead and procurement. Attaching a sanitized sample of token distributions and a simple infra sketch by EOD.

—Samir Shah
VP Product, MediGen Health
samir.shah@medigen.com

Attachments: medigen-token-sample.csv, medigen-network-sketch.png
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: samir.shah@medigen.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-16T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment safeguards & observed SLA thresholds - follow-up

Samir —

Appreciate the details. A couple of technical notes from our infra perspective that affect the recommendation:

- "No co-tenant access to memory/KV cache": we can provide Dedicated pools with single-customer allocation at the GPU-card level. That will remove noisy-neighbor risk for KV cache and per-token jitter, but increases unit costs versus multi-tenant Hosted.
- For P95 < 120ms at 1.1k sustained QPS on 512-token requests, we'll need to size a minimum of 8 x A100-class GPUs with continuous batching and short-prefix caching. If bursts to 1.5k are frequent we recommend burst capacity (hot spare capacity) rather than overprovisioning permanently.
- Private VPC option: offers network-level isolation and customer KMS integration; however, on-prem (air-gapped) deployment would require an abbreviated on-prem package and a longer lead time for validation (SIEM/KMS integration).

I'll put together a short ops-cost delta (expected monthly committed cost vs hosted consumption) and a small appendix on the technical guardrails (KV cache isolation, eviction policies, and fallbacks).

Requested from you: the sanitized token sample and the network sketch you mentioned so we can run a quick sizing simulation. Also please confirm whether your Security team requires a physical single-tenant GPU card or if single-tenant pool (no sharing at the instance level) is sufficient.

If helpful we can run a 2-week Dedicated PoC with agreed SLOs and an automatic rollback to Hosted if we see degradation.

Best —
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
